# ledger_occurrence (Data Source)

Finds one dated occurrence of a commitment, which is what a deferral plan hangs off. Look it up either by its `id`, or by `commitment_id` and the reporting `month` (a commitment has at most one occurrence in a month).

**Occurrences are derived by Ledger, not configured.** It generates them from the commitment's schedule and may rewrite an unpaid one in place or cancel and recreate it after a terms change, so an identifier found here can stop being the one in use. Reading a month makes Ledger materialise the commitment's occurrences through it; months more than 60 months after the current month are refused, and a month before the commitment's start or after its end has none (the lookup fails and says so).

The payment state (status, paid and outstanding amounts) is **derived on every read** from payment evidence and dates in the reporting time zone and can change between two reads. Amounts are exact decimal strings in the occurrence's currency; evidence in other currencies is listed in `unconverted_currencies` and never converted or summed.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# By commitment and reporting month (a commitment has at most one occurrence in a month) ...
data "ledger_occurrence" "september" {
  commitment_id = ledger_commitment.hosting.id
  month         = "2026-09"
}

# ... or by identifier.
data "ledger_occurrence" "known" {
  id = "01JD3Y4C8V9M2Q7W5R6T0XZBNC"
}

# The payment state is derived by Ledger on every read; it is not a guarantee of anything.
output "september_status" {
  value = "${data.ledger_occurrence.september.status}: ${data.ledger_occurrence.september.outstanding_amount} ${data.ledger_occurrence.september.currency} outstanding"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `commitment_id` (String) The commitment (from the `ledger_commitment` resource or data source). With `month`, finds the occurrence.
- `id` (String) The occurrence's Ledger identifier. Set it to look the occurrence up by identifier.
- `include_cancelled` (Boolean) With `commitment_id` and `month`: also consider an occurrence Ledger cancelled (default `false`). A cancelled occurrence owes nothing and takes no plan.
- `month` (String) The reporting month, `YYYY-MM`, in which the occurrence is due. With `commitment_id`, finds the occurrence.

### Read-Only

- `amount` (String) The amount due, an exact decimal string in currency.
- `cancelled_at` (String) When Ledger cancelled the occurrence (RFC 3339, UTC), or null.
- `cancelled_reason` (String) out_of_range, terms_change or commitment_deleted, or null.
- `currency` (String) The ISO 4217 currency of the occurrence.
- `due_date` (String) The due date, YYYY-MM-DD.
- `grace_until` (String) End of the grace period you recorded for an overdue occurrence, or null.
- `outstanding_amount` (String) What the occurrence still owes, an exact decimal string in currency; zero when paid or cancelled.
- `paid_amount` (String) The payment evidence in the occurrence's currency, an exact decimal string (zero when none).
- `status` (String) The derived payment status today: paid, partially_paid, upcoming, due, overdue, not_recorded or cancelled.
- `timing` (String) upcoming, due, overdue or not_recorded for an unpaid occurrence; null when paid or cancelled.
- `unconverted_currencies` (List of String) Currencies of evidence that is not in the occurrence's currency: not counted, never converted.
- `version` (Number) The occurrence's version; it also moves with every payment-state change.
- `within_grace` (Boolean) True while an overdue occurrence is within its recorded grace period.
